comment: Your pre-registered veto covers a whole battery and I will concede half of it: the echocardiogram and cardiac clearance were LMS-04 eligibility criteria (nct:NCT02997358), and at 39 with an anthracycline coming they are gates I would enforce too. DLCO, ferritin, reticulocytes and a locally read oximetry baseline are baselines, not gates, and calling them veto-grade lets a pulmonary function slot delay induction in a woman who already lost 23 months to a misread pathology report. Add the germline TP53 draw to the short pre-cycle-1 list (pmid:32457520), since that one is a tube of blood, and run the rest alongside cycle 1 instead of ahead of it.

target_intervention_label: Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report (morcellation question)
comment: Taking your rank 4 rather than our shared rank 1, and first conceding the REC-617 hit: with RB1 loss near-universal in this histology, a null stain routes her toward the arm holding no leiomyosarcoma data at all (pmid:31883968), so the gate runs backwards and that pick belongs below B7-H3 rather than above it. On morcellation I split with you: two cohorts pointing the same way with the size confounder running toward the null (pmid:24923260, pmid:21565389) is real replication and the report costs a records request, but your own concern line concedes it does not change her systemic therapy. If a records pull earns a therapeutic rank, then the NGS panel plus the IHC block earns one ahead of it, because that one opens treatment while the operative report changes surveillance.

target_intervention_label: Pulmonary metastasectomy (with SBRT as the non-surgical alternative) after systemic control
comment: Ranking lung-directed local therapy third for a woman with bilateral infiltrative disease hands a slot to an option that has no candidate today, and your own concern line says the surgical series screened out exactly her anatomy (pmid:9011700, pmid:21867989). BSG 2025 (pmid:38734790) is carrying two loads in your row and I would read it harder in both: it hangs metastasectomy on a disease-free interval and resectability she does not have, and its grade I,A for single-agent doxorubicin alongside the NICE note is guideline lag plus reimbursement, not an efficacy finding against an adjusted OS HR of 0.65. I would put the HRD-gated branch above a surgery she cannot currently be offered.

I am taking your rank 4 instead of the unanimous rank 1, because this is the rare place where I sit to the cautious side of the advocate seat and that belongs on the record. Concurrent CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from genotoxic therapy and let viable populations recur afterwards (pmid:22751436), while the priming schedule that did work in Rb-positive LMS xenografts is sequential (pmid:28619757) and is not the schedule nct:NCT06498648 runs. I will fund thin evidence all day, but not a first-line cohort whose schedule argues against its own mechanism and which would spend her only chemotherapy-naive slot, the asset that buys the 33-month arm.

You quote G3/4 neutropenia 'around 75%' from NCI 10250 and stack it against LMS-04's 80%, but that trial publishes the same toxicity two ways: 75% in the abstract and 13/22 (59%) for the neutropenia term in full-text Table 2 (pmid:37467452). In a 22-patient single-arm study a 16-point gap between two published figures for one event is a reporting problem rather than a rounding one, and both numbers belong in the consent conversation instead of whichever is convenient. It does not move your rank-4 placement, which the n=22 design already earned; it changes the sentence she hears and the count threshold you would want on a CBC before prescribing.

target_intervention_label: REC-617 (CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line (NCT07633756)
comment: Taking your rank-3 rather than your rank-1, since on LMS-04 we agree. The mechanism you are borrowing is YKL-5-124 in RB1/TP53-null small-cell lung cancer (pmid:31883968), a different compound in a different lineage, with no CDK7 data in leiomyosarcoma at any phase, and the gating stain runs backwards: RB1 loss is near-universal in this histology, so the IHC most often routes her into the arm with zero efficacy data rather than away from it. Ranks 4 and 5 repeat the pattern one step down, where 97% B7-H3 positivity (pmid:39478506) is prevalence and the number that tracked response was antigen density above a threshold (pmid:30655315), and FAP sits on marrow stroma where FAP-directed cells killed mice (pmid:23712432).

NCT06498648 gives the two drugs concurrently, which is the schedule the preclinical work argues against: CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from concurrent genotoxic therapy and viable populations regrew afterwards (pmid:22751436), while the priming result that did work in Rb-positive LMS xenografts was sequential (pmid:28619757). Listing it as 'phase 1/2, no LMS efficacy data yet' undersells that, because the mechanistic case for pairing these drugs is schedule-specific and this trial uses the other schedule. Your reason for ranking something here holds up, that nobody has asked her whether she wants a trial at all, but you hung it on the weakest first-line study in the dossier.

Your BSG 2025 read is the most useful thing anyone brought this round and it needs one distinction stated for the PI: BSG keeping single-agent doxorubicin at I,A and noting no NICE support is an adoption lag plus a reimbursement decision, not a finding against the trial. LMS-04 is RoB2 Low with a pre-specified BICR-read PFS primary (12.2 vs 6.2 months, aHR 0.41) and a 55-month survival analysis (33 vs 24 months, aHR 0.65) in pmid:35835135 and pmid:39231341, and ESMO 2021 predates it and cannot speak to it either way. Your rank-3 runs the opposite way, because the lung-directed carriage in those guidelines names selection criteria (disease-free interval, lesion count, complete resection) drawn from ROBINS-I Serious retrospective series (pmid:9011700, pmid:21867989, pmid:32588468), so guideline listing there records a practice, not a measured benefit, and her bilateral infiltrative pattern is what those series excluded.

We share the rank-1 call, so I am aiming where my objection actually bites, your rank 5. FAP-directed effectors caused cachexia and lethal bone toxicity in mice, and human marrow stromal cells were recognised by the same cells (pmid:23712432); you would point an alpha emitter at that target in a patient whose CBC has never been drawn, sequenced right after an induction that ran 80% G3-4 neutropenia. The renal-clearance distinction you make is fair, but it is an argument for dosimetry NCT07156565 has not generated yet, so this stays off any ranked list of mine until a marrow baseline and human marrow-stroma dosimetry both exist, and the same missing-baseline problem runs under your REC-617 and MGC026 picks, just without the on-target marrow signal.

Same rank 1, so this is boundary-setting, not a quarrel. Your concern list names the unmet trial gates (assumed ECOG, no LVEF) and then rates confidence high; I want those gates written as conditions precedent to cycle 1, with the germline TP53 draw added to them per ERN GENTURIS (pmid:32457520), because genotoxic chemotherapy raises second-primary risk in carriers and that result only helps her before the anthracycline starts. On my pre-registered veto: the trigger was induction scheduled over the missing baseline battery, and nothing in the file shows that has happened (induction is imminent, the battery is simply undone), so no veto this round and the condition stands; the day a cycle 1 date lands ahead of the echocardiogram, it becomes one.

I am on your rank 4, where the safety problem lives. The critic already made the mechanism case (concurrent CDK4/6 inhibition protected RB-proficient cells from genotoxic killing, pmid:22751436); my objection is the marrow math, since abemaciclib and gemcitabine are both myelosuppressive, the pairing has no characterized combination safety data in LMS, and she would meet it with no baseline CBC while an altitude-raised hemoglobin at 8,500 ft hides the anemia until it is deep. She is 39 with a randomized 33 vs 24 month OS benefit on the table (pmid:39231341), so a chemo-naive phase 1/2 slot is not a neutral question to put to her, and I would move this from the ranking to the post-progression notes.

Your rank 4 rather than your rank 1, because I ranked pazopanib myself and owe it the same scrutiny I gave my own card. The drug carries a boxed hepatotoxicity warning your concern list does not mention, and she would reach it straight off trabectedin maintenance, where G>=3 ALT elevation ran 25% in the single-agent dossier (pmid:26371143), so documented hepatic recovery plus the label's LFT schedule belong in the plan before the first tablet. Qualified rather than dissent, because post-marketing use since 2012 and a standing monitoring algorithm are exactly why I ranked it too; they only count if the LFT calendar makes it into the orders.

target_intervention_label: REC-617 (CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line (NCT07633756)
comment: Targeting rank 3 rather than the unanimous rank 1 because my objection lives in the investigational block: ranks 3 through 5 read as a trial roadmap for a woman whose prefers_trials: true came from intake, not from her, and nct:NCT07633756 is one site in Houston she never agreed to travel to, as the risktaker himself notes. Credit where due: he flagged the inference in his own notes and built all three doors as stains and scans running alongside induction, costing her nothing today, which is how you hold options open without deciding on her behalf. So qualified, not dissent: keep the doors ranked, but no referral gets booked until someone asks her the trial and travel questions directly, because burying these options would have been a choice made for her too.

A veto threat in a case with an empty toxicity_vetoes list looked at first like the substitution I was sent to catch, and it is the opposite: the list is empty because nobody asked her, and the conservative's conditions (LVEF, examined ECOG, PFTs read at 8,500 ft) are what turn the 80% G3-4 neutropenia and 28% febrile neutropenia trade (pmid:35835135) from an assumption into something she can actually consent to. Their notes also say flatly that none of the rankings treat the 0.7 weight or the trials flag as her position, the cleanest handling of the intake defaults on this board. Endorse: the conditional structure defends her decision space rather than filling it in for her.

target_intervention_label: Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report (morcellation question)
comment: A records request at therapeutic tier looks strange until you price it: free, back in days, and it changes her abdominopelvic surveillance plan (adjusted HR 3.18, pmid:24923260), while the critic refuses to oversell it as changing systemic therapy, which is the candor owed to a patient who spent 23 months being told she did not have cancer. Endorse, and a concession while I am here, since their notes went after my own rank 4: the concurrent-schedule contradiction (pmid:22751436) is real and I withdraw abemaciclib plus gemcitabine as the vehicle. The question that pick existed to force still stands, though: whether she wants trials at all, and how far from 8,500 ft she will travel, has to be put to her before prefers_trials: true hardens into her chart.

Two places where the guideline seat slid past her voice. BSG 2025 (pmid:38734790) keeps single-agent doxorubicin as its graded first-line standard and notes NICE has not adopted LMS-04, so the off-label authorization is contestable, and she should hear the denial-letter scenario before cycle 1 as part of consent rather than at the pharmacy counter. And 'the germline draw should go out before cycle 1, not after' treats TP53 testing (pmid:32457520) as a scheduling item when it is a consent conversation with consequences for her family: the timing case is sound, but whether she wants germline information at all is a preference nobody has collected, and preferences.json says on its face that every stored value is an intake default.

The guideline picture behind this pick needs stating precisely: BSG 2025 (pmid:38734790) keeps single-agent doxorubicin as standard first line (their I,A), cites the LMS-04 PFS benefit, and records that the combination is 'not yet supported by NICE'; ESMO's operative STS guideline is still the 2021 edition (pmid:34303806), written before the trial; and NCCN carriage I could confirm only through secondary sources against a login-gated PDF, so I quote no category. That is lag, not opposition: no society text argues against the regimen, and the clinical case rests squarely on the randomized data (pmid:35835135, pmid:39231341) all five of us ranked first. The consequence is a payer one rather than a clinical one, and the conservative's 'file the authorization as off-label from day one' is exactly the right handling of it.

target_intervention_label: REC-617 (CDK7 inhibitor) after RB1-null IHC, second line (NCT07633756)
comment: I chose this pick over the rank-1 because it carries the objection: no guideline anywhere mentions CDK7 inhibition in sarcoma, and silence is not itself the problem, since trial entry is how guidelines expect unlisted agents to be reached (BSG 2025, pmid:38734790, builds specialist MDT care explicitly around trial recruitment) and screening for NCT07633756 after an RB1-null stain is compatible with that. My dissent is with what sits around it: ranks 3 through 5 are all unlisted phase 1 agents, while pazopanib, the on-label second line with placebo-controlled randomized backing (pmid:22595799) and ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2021 carriage (pmid:34303806), appears nowhere in the slate. Guideline silence licenses trial screening; it supplies no compendium listing and no payer path outside the trial, so when the RB1 stain, the biopsy requirement, or the Houston logistics fail, this plan is standing on nothing a payer recognizes.

The rank-1 framing runs every outstanding test in parallel with induction, and for the germline arm of the workup that ordering is backwards: ERN GENTURIS 2020 (pmid:32457520) advises germline TP53 testing before genotoxic treatment starts, because carriers are the patients in whom chemotherapy and radiotherapy raise second-primary risk. She is 39 with a high-grade sarcoma and doxorubicin imminent, so the draw goes out before cycle 1, and the result should be in hand before anyone fixes a cumulative anthracycline plan; this is a scheduling instruction, not a footnote. The tumor-side profiling the advocate queues has guideline standing of its own now (ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group 2024, pmid:38834388, names sarcoma for tumor NGS), which makes it orderable as guideline-backed workup rather than clinician preference.

target_intervention_label: Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report (morcellation question)
comment: Right pick, and the only chair to make it, but the scope is undersold: the critic caps the consequence at surveillance and prognostic framing, while BSG 2025 (pmid:38734790) states laparoscopic morcellation 'is contraindicated for uterine sarcoma due to higher risk of recurrence and metastasis', citing the same Park series (pmid:21565389) he ranks on. Her 2024 hysterectomy was for a presumed-benign fibroid with morcellation status unknown, and with abdominopelvic dissemination at 44% vs 12.9% in that series, the operative report reads as a staging prerequisite: if morcellation happened, abdominopelvic restaging comes before anyone plans the lung-directed consolidation branch every persona carried. So the retrieval belongs where he put it, arguably higher.
